[Root.GetTitledName],

Word of your interest has reached us. [GetCollegeCharacterIsPartOf] would be honoured to receive you, but none may enter its halls untested. Come to us, and our examiners will see whether the Winds of Magic answer to you. If they do not, there is no shame in it. If they do, the Articles of Imperial Magic are clear: a gifted soul is safest inside our walls, and far from the Witch Hunters' fires.

Signed,
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
I will come and be tested.
On second thought, no.

For a whole day you follow the examiners' tests: staring into candle flames, counting the colours in a prism, holding your breath while a Magister mutters over you. At dusk they exchange a look you already understand. The Winds of Magic pass through you as they pass through a stone. You are thanked, politely, and shown the door.

The tests go badly, and by midday you are sure you have failed. Then an old Magister lays a hand on your brow and frowns. There is a flicker of the gift in you, faint and stubborn. You are warned that you will struggle past the simplest spells, but the College will not turn away anyone who can touch the Winds.

The tests are hard work, but the examiners nod as you go. You have an ordinary gift, they tell you, neither weak nor remarkable, and a College can make a wizard of that with enough years and discipline. You are entered in the rolls before the day is out.

The tests come surprisingly easily. Candle flames lean towards you and the prism throws colours no one else can see. The examiners hardly need to confer. You have a natural gift for the Winds of Magic, and they enter your name in the rolls of the College at once.

You have barely begun the first test when the candles gutter and the prism cracks in its frame. Half the day is not over before the examiners excuse themselves, and they come back almost falling over each other to offer you a place. The rumour is through the corridors by nightfall: the College has found a prodigy.
At last!
Damn.

Now that you have been accepted into [GetCollegeCharacterIsPartOf], you must choose the Order you will join. Since Teclis taught the first wizards of the Empire, every Imperial wizard studies a single Wind of Magic and no other, for to grasp at all eight is the road to madness and Chaos. Choose well, for you will live with your Wind for the rest of your life.
Choose a Wind.
The Gold Order: Chamon, the Lore of Metal and alchemy.
The Bright Order: Aqshy, the Lore of Fire.
The Amethyst Order: Shyish, the Lore of Death.
The Grey Order: Ulgu, the Lore of Shadows.
The other Orders...
The Amber Order: Ghur, the Lore of Beasts.
The Celestial Order: Azyr, the Lore of the Heavens.
The Light Order: Hysh, the Lore of Light.
The Jade Order: Ghyran, the Lore of Life.
Back to the first Orders.

The [GetCollegeOrderCharacterIsPartOf] has fallen on hard times. No [GetCollegeOrderRankIsPartOf] of the Order is free to take a student, so you must master your Wind alone, from books and from your own mistakes. It will be harder and more dangerous, but a student who teaches himself is noticed.

As part of your introduction to the [GetCollegeOrderCharacterIsPartOf] you are presented to [potential_teacher.GetSocietyRank] [potential_teacher.GetFirstName], who will be your teacher for the next years of study. [potential_teacher.GetSheHeCap] looks you over without a word, then hands you a list of books to read by morning.

Your teacher will not finish your training. The [GetCollegeOrderCharacterIsPartOf] has no other [GetCollegeOrderRankIsPartOf] free to take you on, so you must master your Wind alone. It will be harder, but a student who teaches himself is noticed.

Your teacher will not finish your training. The [GetCollegeOrderCharacterIsPartOf] has given you to [potential_teacher.GetSocietyRank] [potential_teacher.GetFirstName] for the rest of your studies. [potential_teacher.GetSheHeCap] reads your old teacher's notes on you, sighs, and tells you to start again from the beginning.
I have much to learn.
I need no teacher. This is a chance for greatness!
Perhaps another Wind would suit me better.

Every Magister of [GetCollegeCharacterIsPartOf] must take students, and the Order has sent you a new one. [From.GetTitledName] stands at your door with an armful of books and a look of terrified hope.
Listen well and you will go far in the [GetCollegeOrderCharacterIsPartOf].

You have been with [GetCollegeCharacterIsPartOf] for some time, and it is clear that no one rises in the Orders on talent alone. A wizard must make a name for himself: through powerful friends at court, through bold discoveries, or through deeds on the battlefields of the Empire.
I will win them over with words.
I will push the boundaries of magic.
My spells will be seen on the battlefield.
Perhaps another time.

[Root.GetTitledName],

I have watched your progress for some time, and it is clear to me that your talents have not been properly recognised. A word from me in the right ear and you would be promoted. In return, I would ask only that you remember who spoke for you.

Signed,
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
A sound bargain.
I will rise on my own merits.

[Root.GetTitledName],

I gladly accept your help, and I will not forget it.

Signed,
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
Excellent.

[Root.GetTitledName],

Thank you for your offer, but I believe it best that I advance by my own merits.

Signed,
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
Oh well.
A Duel of Spells

[college_patriarch.GetSocietyRank] [college_patriarch.GetFirstName] does not rise from behind [college_patriarch.GetHerHis] desk. "You overreach yourself, [Root.GetSocietyRank]. You wish to lead the [GetCollegeOrderCharacterIsPartOf]? Then you will have to take it from me, before the whole Order, in the duelling hall."\n\nA formal challenge will cost you dearly in favours and influence, win or lose.
Then let the Order watch.
Perhaps it is better to wait.

The Magisters of the Order line the duelling hall in silence. [college_patriarch.GetFirstName] opens with a probing spell, testing your wards, and you let [college_patriarch.GetHerHim] spend [college_patriarch.GetHerHis] strength. Then you strike. The Wind tears through the old wizard's defences and throws [college_patriarch.GetHerHim] across the flagstones. When the smoke clears, the Magisters bow, to you.
The seat is mine.

[college_patriarch.GetFirstName] meets your challenge with an air of unquestioned confidence. Every spell you throw is caught, turned and sent back at you, until you lie on the flagstones with your robes smouldering and the whole Order looking down at you. It will be a long time before anyone in the College forgets this.
I would be angry, if I were not so humiliated.

[college_challenger.GetSocietyRank] [college_challenger.GetFirstName] has laid a formal challenge before the [GetCollegeOrderCharacterIsPartOf]. [college_challenger.GetSheHeCap] claims that you are no longer fit to lead the Order and demands that the matter be settled the old way, with a duel of spells in front of every Magister of the Wind.
I accept. Let the pup learn [college_challenger.GetHerHis] place.
Have the challenge struck from the rolls. Quietly.
I am tired. Let [college_challenger.GetHerHim] have the seat.

[college_challenger.GetFirstName] comes at you with all the fire of youth, and you have fought such duels before. You let [college_challenger.GetHerHim] wear [college_challenger.GetHerHim]self out against your wards, then end it with a single spell. The challenger is carried from the hall, and the Order remembers why you lead it.

You have fought such duels before, but not for many years. [college_challenger.GetFirstName]'s spells are faster than you remember spells being, and when your wards finally break the whole Order sees you fall. You leave the hall a Lord Magister, and someone else sits in your chair.
The seat remains mine.
It is over.

[From.GetTitledName] has signed the Articles of Imperial Magic. By this decree magic within the Empire is no longer the crime of hedge-wizards and witches but a discipline under Imperial law. Eight Orders, one for each of the Winds of Magic, are to be founded in [From.Capital.GetName] under the authority of the [From.GetTitle]. Their wizards must be licensed, must study one Wind only, and must march with the armies of the Empire when called. Those who practise outside the Colleges remain the Witch Hunters' business.

[From.GetTitledName] has decreed new laws on magic in [From.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. A College of Magic is to be founded in [From.Capital.GetName] under the authority of the [From.GetTitle], to train the gifted in the eight Winds of Magic and to keep their power in the service of the realm. Those who practise outside it remain criminals.
A new age of learning begins.
Excellent.
This is horrible. Witchcraft, licensed by the crown!
The College Stores

You have arrived at the stores of [GetCollegeCharacterIsPartOf]. Everything a wizard could need is kept here, at no cost, provided you fill out the correct form in triplicate and obtain the proper seals. The quartermaster peers at you over his spectacles and waits.
Battle equipment.
Robes and regalia.
Books and instruments.
Leave.
Battle Equipment

Battle wizards of the Colleges march with every state army, and the stores keep them armed: staffs to focus the Winds, rings of power, and the Power Stones each Order makes from its own Wind, which hold a spell ready for the moment it is needed.
A Power Stone of my Wind.
A basic staff.
A good staff.
A fine staff.
A ring of power.
Back.
Robes and Regalia

The robes of the Orders are cut in the colours of their Winds and woven with wards against the Winds' backlash. Amulets turn aside blades and curses, and the heads of the Orders may draw the circlet of a Patriarch.
Robes of my Order.
A warding amulet.
The Patriarch's circlet.
Back.
Books and Instruments
The libraries of the Orders are guarded jealously, and only a Magister may take a copy of his Order's grimoire from the shelves. For lesser work there are lenses, scales and magnifying eyeglasses.
The grimoire of my Wind.
Magnifying eyeglasses.
Back.

[Root.GetTitledName],

The [From.GetCollegeOrderCharacterIsPartOf] has long served your house, and its wizards pass through [Root.Capital.GetName] often. I ask that you grant the Order a house of its own here, under your protection: a library, a workshop and a few rooms for travelling Magisters. The Order would remember the kindness, and so would I.

Your servant,
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
Let the Order have its house.
I will not have wizards gathering under my roof.

[Root.GetTitledName],

The [Root.GetCollegeOrderCharacterIsPartOf] shall have its house in [From.Capital.GetName]. See that it does nothing to make me regret it.

[From.GetTitledName]
Excellent.

[Root.GetTitledName],

I have considered your request and must refuse it. The common folk already mutter about witchcraft at my court, and I will not give them a building to point at.

[From.GetTitledName]
So be it.
